exposure: Female cancer survivor status (diagnosed before age 40)
cohort: The study included 1,629 female cancer survivors diagnosed before age 40 years with a first singleton pregnancy after diagnosis, compared to 8,899 age-, deprivation-, and year-matched controls from the general population.
finding: Female cancer survivors had an increased risk of premature delivery and postpartum haemorrhage, but their offspring were not at increased risk for low birth weight or congenital abnormalities.
mod_finding: Operative delivery was more common in cancer survivors, but rates approached those of controls with more recent diagnoses, indicating a normalisation of delivery method over time.
gest_age: <37 weeks of gestation, small for gestational age
